saints.name: St. Polycarp
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A disciple of the Apostle John and bishop of Smyrna, who at the stake refused to revile the Christ he had served fourscore and six years…
biography: Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, was a disciple of the Apostle John; Irenaeus, who heard him as a boy, treasured his memory of John and of others who had seen the Lord. With Clement of Rome and Ignatius of Antioch he ranks among the Apostolic Fathers.

In old age he went to Rome to confer with Pope Anicetus on the date of Easter, keeping the Asian custom of the fourteenth of Nisan; neither won the other, yet they parted in peace, Anicetus honouring him in his church.

Arrested about the year 155 and pressed to curse Christ, he answered, 'Eighty and six years have I served him, and he has done me no wrong; how then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?' He was burned at the stake and, when the fire would not touch him, slain with a dagger.

The church of Smyrna's letter recounting his death is the earliest martyrdom narrative outside Scripture, and the first witness to the veneration of a martyr's relics; the faithful gathered his bones as 'more precious than precious stones' and kept the birthday of his martyrdom.
saints.knownFor: His martyrdom at Smyrna and his link to the age of the Apostles.
